Choke-point design: privacy.go is the single definition of CacheControlPrivateNoStore = 'private, no-store', and the two graph response writers writeJSON (success) and WriteError (every typed error; WriteAPIError and GraphCapability.WriteDisabled funnel through it) stamp it, so every family, list and detail, success and error and the disabled 503, is covered without editing a handler and a newly added family inherits the contract automatically. Ordering is load-bearing: SetPrivateNoStore MUST precede WriteHeader because Go freezes the header map at the status line, so a later Set is silently dropped with no compile or runtime error; two of the three adversarial privacy_test.go unit tests exist specifically to fail if that ordering is inverted. TIER SPLIT: the unit tests prove the writers SET the header before commit but, observing only a ResponseRecorder, cannot prove it survives; the live run proves it SURVIVES the full middleware chain to the wire - ./smackerel.sh test e2e --go-run 'TestE2E_GraphResponsesArePrivateNoStore|TestE2E_GraphFamilyJourneyIsReadOnly|TestE2E_ExpiredSessionAndDeniedScope' (2026-07-28T08:31:42Z -> 08:35:39Z, ===PRIVACY_E2E_EXIT=0===): graph-owned 200 detail, 200 list, and 400 typed error each carry EXACTLY 'private, no-store', all 8 canonical manifest paths are no-store-bearing, and the pre-handler 401 carries the global bare 'no-store' from securityHeadersMiddleware. security phase executed directly against source after two dispatched subagent attempts returned no result and made no changes. VERDICT: no security defect; one deliberate design decision reviewed and accepted. (1) ERROR ENVELOPE LEAKAGE - CLEAN: ErrorEnvelope is a closed three-field shape {error:{code,message,field}} and WriteError encodes only literals supplied by call sites, so no stack trace, SQL, table name, or path can reach the wire. (2) AUTH ORDERING - CORRECT with an accepted trade-off: the graph manifest registers INSIDE bearerAuthMiddleware so an unauthenticated caller never reaches the Guard; within that group Guard precedes RequireScope, so an AUTHENTICATED caller lacking knowledge-graph:read sees 503 capability_disabled rather than 403 when the capability is off. That is deliberate and documented at the registration site (a disabled deployment must be honestly present-but-disabled on every known path), the disclosure is bounded to authenticated callers, and the same fact is already visible via the authenticated /api/health graph aggregate. Reordering would contradict the fail-soft contract this packet establishes, so it is ACCEPTED, not changed. (3) EXISTENCE ORACLE - CLOSED and genuinely tested: corpus_authorization_test.go:562 asserts a real seeded id and a certainly-absent id are answered byte-identically for an ungranted caller across nine paths spanning all five families. (4) CACHE PRIVACY ON ERRORS - CORRECT: WriteError calls SetPrivateNoStore BEFORE WriteHeader, which is load-bearing because Go freezes the header map at the status line; WriteAPIError and GraphCapability.WriteDisabled both funnel through WriteError, so every typed error including the disabled 503 carries private, no-store. (5) TEST AUTH PATH - structurally inert in production: the seeded auth_token cookie authenticates only when AuthConfig.Enabled==false; production requires a PASETO v4.public token or WebCredentials, and the cookie carries Secure when Environment==production. NO product or test code was changed, so no gate re-run was required and the recorded build-gate evidence remains current.
